title: The Tree-Climbing Lions of Lake Manyara
excerpt: Lions in trees: Lake Manyara is one of the places in Africa where this unusual behaviour has been seen. Why lions climb and how likely you are to see it.
body:
Lions are not known as climbers. Yet in a few places in Africa, including Lake Manyara and parts of the Serengeti, lions regularly rest in trees.

## Why do they climb?

Nobody knows for sure. Possible reasons:

- Escape from biting flies on the ground.
- A cooler breeze.
- A better view over the area.
- Learned behaviour passed on within a pride.

## How likely are you to see it?

Not guaranteed. Lion numbers in Manyara vary, and they are not always in trees. Guides often ask each other where the lions are. Patience and luck help.

## Other places

Lions in trees are also seen in parts of the Serengeti, and in Uganda's Queen Elizabeth National Park.

## Leopards

If you see a big cat in a tree, it could also be a leopard. See [how to tell cheetah and leopard apart](/blog/cheetah-vs-leopard/) and [leopard facts](/blog/leopard-facts/).
